A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MathFusion work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original model fine-tuning results across six benchmarks, fusion ablations, scaling and error analyses, and repeated-run results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds a 195K-sample experiment, Mosaic-IT comparisons, and an alternative-teacher ablation.

M1.justification: The embedding-based pairing, three fusion strategies, synthesis prompts, and supervised fine-tuning pipeline are retained. The expanded neighbor count and alternative teacher are experimental configurations without a new core method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K/MATH as source data and evaluate GSM8K, MATH, CollegeMath, DeepMind-Mathematics, OlympiadBench-Math, and TheoremQA. The enlarged dataset and new controls reuse this mathematical coverage without adding domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates Mosaic-IT's Primary Strategy alone and mixed with original data in Appendix E and Table 6; v1 only discussed Mosaic-IT. Table 6 also adds DART-Math alongside the teacher controls, while Table 2's comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 195K-sample configuration using neighbors ranked second through fourth alongside the nearest neighbor. Table 6's rewrite control changes from Llama3-8B with 30K original-plus-rewritten samples to Mistral-7B with 15K rewritten samples. Alternative-teacher and 15K/30K Mosaic-IT configurations are added; existing benchmark splits, metrics, and main training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds DeepSeekMath-7B-RL as a solution teacher and revises the rewrite ablation to examine the source of gains. New Appendix E tests concatenation and mixing original data, while the 195K run extends scaling analysis. Existing fusion-component, difficulty, diversity, error, and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains identical three-run results, means, and standard deviations. The paired t-test and p < 0.05 claims are unchanged, moving from Appendix E to F. No new uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds the 195K DeepSeekMath-based result, averaging 49.9, alongside the unchanged 60K result of 47.5. Table 6 adds Mistral-7B rewrite results averaging 20.9, Mosaic-IT results of 13.6 and 15.6, and alternative-teacher MathFusion results of 34.6. The earlier Llama3-8B rewrite result of 23.5 is replaced under different settings, so this is not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of pairing and the three fusion strategies, dataset-union expression, and instruction-following difficulty formula are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction now claims that scaling MathFusion itself can surpass DART-Math with less than one-third of its training data, extending v1's emphasis on combining the two datasets. The three fusion contributions and the abstract's 18.0-point improvement using 45K additional instructions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds the hypothesis that Mosaic-IT's weak results reflect insufficient logical integration between concatenated problems. The limitations now specifically identify stronger teachers such as DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3, and scaling to millions of examples, as underexplored.

D1.justification: V2 adds a Hugging Face collection link and documents construction of the 195K dataset, the alternative solution teacher, and Mosaic-IT data mixtures. It explicitly states that the released dataset contains 60K examples. Existing prompts, hardware, training hyperparameters, and evaluation templates are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to MetaLadder, LEMMA, and OpenMathInstruct-2. It expands the comparison with the already-cited Mosaic-IT, emphasizing logical integration versus concatenation, while retaining the overall related-work structure and positioning.

P1.justification: V2 corrects the title, updates affiliations, edits several passages, clarifies training-data composition, adds an analysis overview and acknowledgements, and inserts an appendix section. Most narrative structure and wording are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a row, and Table 6 is expanded and recaptioned. Figure 4(b,c) changes point colors and marker sizes while retaining the plotted coordinates. The title block adds resource links and icons, and material reflows across pages; other figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The Mosaic-IT controls and alternative-teacher ablation provide useful additional evidence about the source of MathFusion's gains, while the 195K experiment extends scaling evidence. More explicit limitations and access information improve transparency. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of the earlier Llama3-8B rewrite control, although changed settings and absent uncertainty estimates for the new comparisons limit the strength of the improvement.
